_metadata.title: Cluevoyance Unlimited - independent semantic review of the 20-word pilot
_metadata.reviewer_independence: Phases 1-3 were completed and written to disk before pilot-clue-quality-audit.json, pilot-quality-review.md or pilot-review.md were opened. No score in this file was changed after reading the previous audit.
_metadata.method: Every one of the 536 current clues and every one of the 150 removed clues was read individually and scored against the rubric below. Scores are editorial judgement, not computation.

rubric.total: sum of positives minus penalties, range -4 to 10

verdicts.PASS: Both connections >= 1, fair, not padding, and the clue rather than the explanation carries the link.
verdicts.BORDERLINE: A real connection exists but it is one-sided, obscure, or supplied by the explanation. Playable, not dependable.

rubric.difference_from_the_previous_audit: The previous audit used a binary pass/fail with a total >= 6 threshold. This review uses three verdicts, so many clues that scored 6-7 there are recorded as BORDERLINE here rather than as failures. Only PASS counts toward the two-good-clue minimum.

repository_health.eslint: 35 pre-existing problems in src/App.jsx, untouched by this review

headline_findings: The set is closer to ready than to broken. 450 of 536 clues (84.0%) pass independently, and 171 of 190 pairs (90.0%) already carry two clues I would defend.

The 110 clues written after the previous audit pass at 73.6%, against 86.6% for the 426 clues the previous audit had independently scored. That 13.0-point gap is the self-approval bias the previous review predicted in its own caveat, and it is now measured.
19 pairs fall below the two-good-clue minimum on my scoring. Restoring removed clues fixes exactly one of them; the other 18 need new writing.

71 of the 150 removals were clues the previous audit itself passed, cut to satisfy a global repeat ceiling. Per the brief, repetition is a board-generation concern. 23 of those cuts should be reversed.
HONEY + SHADOW, which the previous review upgraded from impossible to solved, is on my reading still the weakest pair in the set: all three clues are new, all three are one-sided, and none passes.

clue_reviews.explanation: A bridge spans the river from one bank to the other.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Both senses land instantly; only demerit is low surprise.

clue_reviews.explanation: You cross a bridge to reach the far bank.
clue_reviews.reasoning: BRIDGE side strong, BANK side leans on "the far bank" supplied by the explanation.

clue_reviews.explanation: A canal has banks on both sides and a bridge over it every mile.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Clean shared setting, both words genuinely present.

clue_reviews.explanation: The crown is royalty and Royal Bank is one of the commonest bank names there is.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Royal Bank is a real institution name; crown is definitional.

clue_reviews.explanation: The Royal Mint belongs to the crown and strikes the coins the banks hand out.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Mint-to-money is immediate; Royal Mint carries the crown.

clue_reviews.explanation: A sovereign is the crowned head of state and also the gold coin a bank once paid out.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Lovely double sense; gold sovereign is UK and historical so recognition dips.

clue_reviews.explanation: Diamonds are kept in a bank vault.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Direct and fair.

clue_reviews.explanation: The diamond heist and the bank job are the same film plot.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Single film-plot image holds both words at once.

clue_reviews.explanation: A diamond goes in a safe and the safe goes in a bank.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Plain but honest.

clue_reviews.explanation: A plane banks into a turn on the power of its engines.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Exploits the aviation sense of BANK properly.

clue_reviews.explanation: A plane banks into a turn, and an engine turns over when it starts.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Two separate idioms on one verb; fair enough.

clue_reviews.explanation: A bank has a drive-through window and an engine is the thing that drives.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Drive-through is a weak reach for BANK; ENGINE side is near-tautology.

clue_reviews.explanation: A fire alarm and a bank alarm are both standard emergency fixtures.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Both are standard fixtures.

clue_reviews.explanation: A firebreak stops a blaze spreading, and to break the bank means to spend everything.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Firebreak plus break-the-bank: two real phrases.

clue_reviews.explanation: Banks keep valuables in safes, and those safes are specifically built to be fireproof.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Fireproof safe is genuine, if quieter.

clue_reviews.explanation: A bank vault holds the money and a burial vault holds the dead.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Burial vault is real but GHOST is one step past it; badly asymmetric.

clue_reviews.explanation: A bank account is the everyday one; a ghost account is the dormant or fake one nobody is behind.
clue_reviews.reasoning: "Ghost account" is not a settled phrase; BANK side does all the work.

clue_reviews.explanation: A ghost town with its abandoned bank and open vault is the stock Western image.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Ghost town is strong; the abandoned bank is scenery the explanation adds.

clue_reviews.explanation: A blood bank stores the blood the heart pumps.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Blood bank is exact and the heart pumps it.

clue_reviews.explanation: You steal from a bank and you steal someone's heart.
clue_reviews.reasoning: One verb, two complete idioms.

clue_reviews.explanation: A trust is a banking arrangement and trust is a matter of the heart.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Both reaches are loose; trust fund is finance-generic.

clue_reviews.explanation: Bees store honey for the winter exactly as a bank stores money.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Storing is a generic verb; honey side is bee behaviour, not language.

clue_reviews.explanation: Robbing a bank is the classic crime, and robbing the hive is the beekeeper's own word for taking the honey.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Bank robbery is instant; robbing the hive is real beekeeper usage.

clue_reviews.explanation: A honey pot holds the honey and a pot of money is what you bank.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Honeypot and pot of money both stand up.

clue_reviews.explanation: A stable is where a horse is kept and a bank is supposed to be financially stable.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Genuine homonym, satisfying on reveal.

clue_reviews.explanation: A horse charges into battle and bank charges are the fees on your account.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Bank charges is everyday; cavalry charge is vivid.

clue_reviews.explanation: You bet on a horse and you bank on a sure thing; both are staking money on an outcome.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Bet on and bank on are a real pair of gambles.

clue_reviews.explanation: Banks hold gold bars and iron bars are what keep a vault shut.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Gold bar and iron bar both concrete.

clue_reviews.explanation: Pig iron is the raw cast metal and a piggy bank is the first bank anyone owns.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Pig iron and piggy bank: the best clue in the BANK block.

clue_reviews.explanation: A bank safe is a box of thick iron.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Serviceable, slightly duplicated by BAR vault imagery.

clue_reviews.explanation: A bank vault is the thing a key is needed for.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Direct.

clue_reviews.explanation: A safe deposit box sits in a bank and opens with the customer's own key.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Safe deposit box is a real object holding both.

clue_reviews.explanation: A bank locks its money away and a key is what opens a lock.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Plain and fair.

clue_reviews.explanation: A floodlight is a lamp and a flood is what happens when a river bursts its banks.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Floodlight and burst banks; two distinct senses of the clue.

clue_reviews.explanation: A streetlight stands on it and a high-street bank stands on it too.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Streetlight is universal; high-street bank is British phrasing.

clue_reviews.explanation: A green light means go and greenbacks are the money a bank holds.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Green light is instant; greenbacks carries the money side.

clue_reviews.explanation: You check your hair in the mirror and you write a check on the bank.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Cheque/check spelling split, and checking in a mirror barely evokes MIRROR.

clue_reviews.explanation: A mirror is silvered glass and silver is the metal banking was built on.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Silvered glass is exact; silver-as-money is real but softer.

clue_reviews.explanation: Banks have a night deposit box, and night is when the moon is out.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Night deposit is genuine though not top-of-mind.

clue_reviews.explanation: A river runs between its banks and Moon River is the song everyone knows.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Moon River plus river bank; clean cultural double.

clue_reviews.explanation: A rose bed is where they are planted and a river bed sits between the banks.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Rose bed and river bed both standard.

clue_reviews.explanation: A rose bursts into bloom and a river bursts its banks.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Bursting banks is the stronger half.

clue_reviews.explanation: A hedge fund is a bank's business and the wild rose is the hedgerow flower.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Hedge fund is good; hedgerow rose is a gardener fact, not a player one.

clue_reviews.explanation: A salt deposit is laid down underground and a bank deposit is paid in over the counter.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Two literal deposits; excellent.

clue_reviews.explanation: Worth your salt is the idiom and net worth is the figure the bank cares about.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Worth your salt and net worth both idiomatic.

clue_reviews.explanation: Roman soldiers were paid in salt, which is where the word salary comes from, and salary is what goes into the bank.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Rests entirely on the sal-/salary etymology the explanation states.

clue_reviews.explanation: A shady bank is where you sit on a hot day, and a shady bank is also a crooked one.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Shady bank works in both directions at once; genuinely witty.

clue_reviews.explanation: A cloud bank is a real formation and a passing cloud is what drags a shadow across the ground.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Cloud bank is a real formation and clouds drag shadows.

clue_reviews.explanation: A river snakes across the country between its two banks.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Snaking river between banks.

clue_reviews.explanation: To snake means to wind along, which is exactly what a river does between its banks.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Same idea as RIVER but the verb carries it.

clue_reviews.explanation: A snake basks in the sun on a warm bank.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Concrete image, fair.

clue_reviews.explanation: Spring break is the holiday and breaking the bank is the idiom for overspending.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Spring break and break the bank.

clue_reviews.explanation: A spring is where water comes out of the ground and a bank is what water runs between.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Honest but flat.

clue_reviews.explanation: A crown and a bridge are both things a dentist fits in your mouth.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Both are dental fittings; the reveal is satisfying.

clue_reviews.explanation: A crown caps one tooth and a bridge spans the gap where others are missing.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Same mechanism, equally fair.

clue_reviews.explanation: An arch is what holds a stone bridge up, and the crown is the architect's name for the very top of it.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Crown-of-an-arch is architect vocabulary, not general knowledge.

clue_reviews.explanation: Diamonds is a card suit and bridge is a card game.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Suit and game in one word.

clue_reviews.explanation: In bridge a suit is named as trumps and diamonds is one of the four that can be.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Correct for bridge; the word now carries loud political noise.

clue_reviews.explanation: Both belong to the same deck of fifty-two.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Valid but a near-restatement of CARD inside the same pair.

clue_reviews.explanation: A ship has a bridge where the captain stands and an engine room below decks.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Bridge and engine room on the same vessel; excellent.

clue_reviews.explanation: A railway bridge is built for the engine to cross.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Railway bridge; direct.

clue_reviews.explanation: Iron bridges and steam engines were both held together with rivets.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Riveted steam engines is enthusiast knowledge; BRIDGE carries it alone.

clue_reviews.explanation: To burn your bridges is the idiom, and burning is what fire does.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Burn your bridges.

clue_reviews.explanation: Crossfire is what you get caught in and crossing is what a bridge is for.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Crossfire and crossing; two clean senses.

clue_reviews.explanation: London Bridge is the one in the nursery rhyme and the Great Fire of London is the city's other famous story.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Two famous London stories; strong if UK-leaning.

clue_reviews.explanation: A toll is what you pay to cross a bridge and a bell tolls for the dead.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Toll bridge and the tolling bell; the death step is short.

clue_reviews.explanation: Crossing over is the gentle word for dying, and crossing over is what you do on a bridge.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Crossing over is exactly the euphemism; very good.

clue_reviews.explanation: The other side is the afterlife, and it is also simply the far end of the bridge.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Equally good but the same metaphor as CROSS OVER.

clue_reviews.explanation: Hearts is a card suit and bridge is a card game.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Suit and game.

clue_reviews.explanation: Cross my heart is the promise and crossing is what a bridge is for.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Cross my heart.

clue_reviews.explanation: A bridge closes a gap and a hole in the heart is a gap surgeons close.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Bridging a gap is literal; the cardiac hole is a fair second step.

clue_reviews.explanation: Winnie-the-Pooh wants honey above everything, and Poohsticks is the game you play from a bridge.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Poohsticks and the honey pot; charming and fair.

clue_reviews.explanation: Honey is what a sweet tooth wants and a bridge is what the dentist fits once the teeth have gone.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Sweet tooth into dental bridge; the causal chain actually works.

clue_reviews.explanation: The Golden Gate is the most famous bridge there is, and golden is the standard word for honey.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Golden Gate is strong; golden honey is colour-level.

clue_reviews.explanation: The bridge of the nose is the bony ridge, and a horse wins by a nose.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Bridge of the nose and win by a nose.

clue_reviews.explanation: A violin has a bridge holding the strings up and a bow strung with horsehair.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Needs to know the bow is horsehair; BRIDGE side is solid.

clue_reviews.explanation: A wooden bridge is the oldest kind and the wooden horse is how Troy fell.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Wooden bridge and the wooden horse of Troy.

clue_reviews.explanation: A bridge is built out of iron girders.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Literal.

clue_reviews.explanation: Iron bridges are held together by thousands of rivets.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Literal and fair here, unlike the ENGINE pair.

clue_reviews.explanation: An iron bridge rusts, which is why they are forever being repainted.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Correct, if unexciting.

clue_reviews.explanation: A song has a bridge in the middle and is written in a key.
clue_reviews.reasoning: A song has a bridge and is in a key; excellent.

clue_reviews.explanation: A key is a low-lying island and bridges are what string the Florida Keys together.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Florida Keys strung together by bridges.

clue_reviews.explanation: A stone bridge stands on its arch, and the keystone is the wedge at the top that holds the arch shut.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Keystone holds the arch; very satisfying.

clue_reviews.explanation: A beam bridge is the plainest kind there is and a beam of light is the plainest kind of light.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Beam bridge and beam of light; the plainest word doing double duty.

clue_reviews.explanation: A rainbow is made of light and in Norse myth it is the bridge to Asgard.
clue_reviews.reasoning: A rainbow is made of light and arcs like a bridge; Bifrost is a bonus.

clue_reviews.explanation: Tower Bridge is the famous crossing and a lighthouse is a tower built to hold a light.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Tower Bridge and lighthouse.

clue_reviews.explanation: An arch and its reflection make a double, which is the only thing a mirror ever gives you.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Only works once you supply the water the explanation supplies.

clue_reviews.explanation: Venice is a city of bridges and Venetian glass made the mirrors Europe wanted.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Venetian mirror glass is an art-history fact, not a player instinct.

clue_reviews.explanation: Over the moon means delighted, and over is where a bridge takes you.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Over the moon is strong; OVER is a weak, colourless clue word.

clue_reviews.explanation: A bridge is an arch, and the moon arcs across the sky and shows an arc when it is a crescent.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Arch of a bridge and the moon arc.

clue_reviews.explanation: A crescent is the shape of the moon and the shape of a single-span bridge over the water.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Crescent bridge is the explanation invention; also restates ARCH.

clue_reviews.explanation: A rose arch is a garden structure and an arch is what holds a bridge up.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Rose arch is a real garden structure.

clue_reviews.explanation: A compass rose is printed on every chart, and the bridge is where the ship's officer reads it.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Compass rose read from the ship bridge; elegant.

clue_reviews.explanation: A bridge ices over before the road does, which is why the salt lorry goes across it first.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Bridges ice first and get salted first; genuinely informative.

clue_reviews.explanation: Road salt is what rots the steel in a bridge.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Road salt rots bridge steel.

clue_reviews.explanation: An old salt is a sailor and the bridge is where he stands.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Old salt on the bridge; two ship senses meeting.

clue_reviews.explanation: The troll lives under the bridge in its shadow.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Troll evokes BRIDGE hard and SHADOW barely.

clue_reviews.explanation: Under the bridge is where the shadow is and where people shelter.
clue_reviews.reasoning: A bare preposition; the shadow link is scene-setting.

clue_reviews.explanation: A bridge arch throws a black shadow on the water below.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Any solid object throws a shadow; nothing specific to SHADOW here.

clue_reviews.explanation: A river snakes across the country and a bridge is what gets you over it.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Snaking river, bridge over it.

clue_reviews.explanation: The cables slung across a suspension bridge hang in long snaking curves.
clue_reviews.reasoning: The snake reading is the explanation simile, not the word meaning.

clue_reviews.explanation: A rope bridge is the one that sways, and a rope lying in the grass is what gets mistaken for a snake.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Rope bridge, and a rope mistaken for a snake; both real.

clue_reviews.explanation: A suspension bridge hangs from cables and a car's suspension rides on springs.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Suspension bridge and car suspension; the best kind of double.

clue_reviews.explanation: A bridge crosses water and a spring is where that water starts.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Fair, flat.

clue_reviews.explanation: A long bridge bounces underfoot the way a spring does.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Bridge bounce is a stretch the explanation has to argue for.

clue_reviews.explanation: The crown jewels are diamonds.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Crown jewels; definitional for both.

clue_reviews.explanation: A diamond is set into the band of a crown.
clue_reviews.reasoning: A stone is set into the band; literal.

clue_reviews.explanation: A crown sparkles because of the diamonds in it.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Circular: the crown sparkles only because of the diamond. Near-padding.

clue_reviews.explanation: The crown wheel is the big gear in a car's back axle that the engine finally turns.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Crown wheel is drivetrain jargon; almost no player reaches CROWN from WHEEL.

clue_reviews.explanation: The Royal Train carries the Crown and an engine is what pulls it.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Royal Train is UK-specific and secondary; ENGINE does all the work.

clue_reviews.explanation: A piston is the heart of an engine and the top face of one is called its crown.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Piston crown is specialist mechanic vocabulary. Unfair and unrecognisable.

clue_reviews.explanation: Ring of Fire is a familiar name, and a crown is a ring worn on the head.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Ring of Fire and a ring on the head.

clue_reviews.explanation: A crown of candles is worn at midwinter and a candle is a small flame carried about.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Saint Lucia crown of candles is real but Scandinavian; the flame side is solid.

clue_reviews.explanation: Crowns are made of gold and firelight is a golden colour.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Firelight-is-golden is a colour association, which the brief excludes.

clue_reviews.explanation: Hamlet opens with the ghost of a king demanding his stolen crown be avenged.
clue_reviews.reasoning: One play carries the murdered king, the stolen crown and the ghost.

clue_reviews.explanation: A king wears the crown and the ghost of a dead king is the oldest story there is.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Crowned king and the ghost of a dead king.

clue_reviews.explanation: The castle is where the crown lives and where its ghosts are said to walk.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Standard setting for both; fair if unoriginal.

clue_reviews.explanation: The Queen of Hearts is the card and a queen is who wears the crown.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Queen of Hearts.

clue_reviews.explanation: The King of Hearts is in every deck and a king is crowned.
clue_reviews.reasoning: King of Hearts; structurally identical to QUEEN within this pair.

clue_reviews.explanation: Hearts is a card suit and the crowned royals are the face cards.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Suit plus crowned face cards; the third clue on one idea.

clue_reviews.explanation: The queen bee rules the hive that makes the honey and a queen is who wears the crown.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Queen bee and crowned queen; the hive makes the honey.

clue_reviews.explanation: Royal jelly is what the hive feeds its future queen, and royal is what a crown makes you.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Royal jelly is exact.

clue_reviews.explanation: Mead is wine made from honey and it is what got drunk in the crowned head's hall.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Mead-to-honey is solid; mead-to-crown needs the mead-hall picture supplied.

clue_reviews.explanation: The Triple Crown is the prize a horse wins by taking all three of the great races.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Triple Crown; the single best fit in the CROWN block.

clue_reviews.explanation: The crowned monarch rides in a carriage pulled by horses.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Coronation coach; concrete.

clue_reviews.explanation: The chess knight is a horse and the king beside it is the piece wearing the crown.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Knight is a horse, king wears the crown; neat and fair.

clue_reviews.explanation: The Iron Throne is the seat and the crown is what goes with it.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Iron Throne; widely known and both words present.

clue_reviews.explanation: The Man in the Iron Mask is a story about who is entitled to wear the crown.
clue_reviews.reasoning: The Man in the Iron Mask is about who may wear the crown.

clue_reviews.explanation: Ruling with an iron fist is what a crowned despot does.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Iron fist is strong; the crowned despot is the explanation adding a monarch.

clue_reviews.explanation: The keys to the kingdom is the phrase and the crown is what rules the kingdom.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Keys to the kingdom and the crown that rules it.

clue_reviews.explanation: The crown jewels are locked in the Tower of London and the Ceremony of the Keys locks it every night.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Crown jewels in the Tower is strong; Ceremony of the Keys is UK trivia.

clue_reviews.explanation: The crown jewels are kept under lock and key.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Lock and key is a set phrase; CROWN only arrives via the jewels in the explanation.

clue_reviews.explanation: The Statue of Liberty wears a spiked crown and holds up a torch of light.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Spiked crown and raised torch on one statue.

clue_reviews.explanation: A halo is a ring of light that sits exactly where a crown would.
clue_reviews.reasoning: A ring of light sitting exactly where a crown would.

clue_reviews.explanation: Corona is Latin for crown, which is where coronation comes from, and the sun's corona is a ring of light.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Corona is literally crown and is also a ring of light; best kind of wordplay.

clue_reviews.explanation: The wicked queen wears the crown and asks the mirror on the wall who is fairest.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Snow White: the crowned queen and the talking mirror.

clue_reviews.explanation: A vanity is the table with the mirror and vanity is the sin a crown encourages.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Vanity table is strong for MIRROR; vanity-as-royal-sin is asserted, not evoked.

clue_reviews.explanation: A gilt mirror frame and a crown are both gold.
clue_reviews.reasoning: A gilt frame is incidental. Colour/material padding.

clue_reviews.explanation: A halo ring often appears around the moon, and a crown is a ring that sits above the head the same way.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Lunar halo and the ring on a head; works in both directions.

clue_reviews.explanation: Diana was the Roman goddess of the moon and Diana was the princess in the tiara.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Roman moon goddess and the princess in the tiara; excellent double.

clue_reviews.explanation: A crown of thorns is the famous one and thorns are what a rose is armed with.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Crown of thorns and the armed rose.

clue_reviews.explanation: The Tudor rose is the emblem of the English crown.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Tudor rose is the crown emblem; solid if UK history.

clue_reviews.explanation: A garland of roses worn on the head is a crown in all but name.
clue_reviews.reasoning: A garland worn on the head is a crown in all but name.

clue_reviews.explanation: Gandhi's Salt March was a march against the Crown's monopoly on salt.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Salt March against the Crown monopoly; both words genuinely present.

clue_reviews.explanation: An old salt serves in the navy and the navy belongs to the Crown.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Old salt in the navy, Royal Navy under the Crown; two hops but fair ones.

clue_reviews.explanation: The salt tax was one of the crown's great sources of revenue.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Salt tax as crown revenue; restates the GANDHI idea.

clue_reviews.explanation: The crown of a tree is its canopy, and the canopy is what throws the shade.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Crown of a tree is the canopy and the canopy throws the shade.

clue_reviews.explanation: The heir spends a lifetime waiting in the shadow of the crown.
clue_reviews.reasoning: In the shadow of the crown; the idiom is real.

clue_reviews.explanation: A crown sits on the head and the head is what casts the shadow.
clue_reviews.reasoning: Literal and fair.

clue_reviews.explanation: Egyptian pharaohs wore a rearing cobra on the front of the crown.
clue_reviews.reasoning: The uraeus on the pharaoh crown.

repeat_analysis.separation_note: Repetition is reported here strictly as a future board-generation concern. No clue in this review was downgraded for appearing in another pair, and no restoration was refused on that ground.
repeat_analysis.ceiling_observed: No clue text is used more than four times. The pre-repair set reached eleven (GOLD). A hard ceiling of four was evidently enforced during the repair.
repeat_analysis.finding: The ceiling was enforced by deleting clues rather than by rewriting them. 71 clues the previous audit had passed were cut on that ground alone, and 23 of them are good enough to restore. At 190 pairs a ceiling of four is defensible; at 1,225 pairs it is the single largest scaling risk in the dataset.

systematic_bias_in_the_previous_review: Self-approval on the new clues. The previous review states the risk plainly in its own caveat and then reports 100% passing anyway. Measured against an independent pass, the 110 self-approved clues run 13.0 points below the clues that had been independently scored.

A binary threshold hides the weak middle. A total of 6 out of 10 was recorded as a pass with no further mark, so a one-sided clue and an excellent one both appear as "pass" in the headline figure. 50 of my 56 disagreements are clues scoring 6-8 there.

The mechanical rubric is under-weighted on asymmetry. The rule requires each connection to be >= 1, which lets a 2/1 clue through at full credit. Asymmetry is the most common real defect in this set and the rubric does not price it.
Repetition was treated as a quality defect rather than a board-generation constraint, which cost 71 clues, several of them good.
systematic_bias_in_my_own_review: I am stricter on lateral and specialist clues than the previous reviewer, which will read as harsh on pairs like CROWN + ENGINE where nothing better may exist.
I score three ways rather than two, so my BORDERLINE count is not comparable to a failure count and should not be read as one.
I did not playtest. Fairness and recognizability are my estimate of a general audience, and a real audience may find some clues I marked obscure perfectly ordinary, or the reverse.
I applied a UK/US knowledge split as a recognizability penalty in several places (STREET, CABINET, WING, SOVEREIGN). If the audience is primarily British those penalties are too harsh.

final_verdict.qualification: Small in volume, not small in significance. 18 pairs need new clues written - roughly 25 to 30 clues - and the generation method needs one process change, not a redesign.
required_before_a_50_word_test: Write new clues for the 18 pairs that cannot reach two independently passing clues by restoration. HONEY + SHADOW, CROWN + ENGINE, HEART + SHADOW, BRIDGE + SHADOW and BRIDGE + MIRROR are the hardest and should be written first.
Apply the 13 recommended restorations; they are free quality, already written, and every one keeps its pair at or under five clues.

Fix the five outright failures: CROWN+ENGINE PISTON, DIAMOND+GHOST FOREVER, GHOST+SPRING JACK, HORSE+SNAKE VENOM, MIRROR+ROSE VANITY. HORSE+KEY GATE is a sixth - it duplicates STABLE with the same proverb and very nearly the same explanation text.
Separate authoring from approval permanently. The measured 13-point gap between self-approved and independently-scored clues is the strongest evidence this pilot produced.
Decide the repeat ceiling before generating, not after, and enforce it by rewriting rather than deleting.
final_verdict.what_is_genuinely_good: The top of the set is better than it needs to be. PIG for BANK+IRON, DEPOSIT for BANK+SALT, STONE for BRIDGE+KEY, NARCISSUS for MIRROR+SPRING, CORONA for CROWN+LIGHT and DOUBT for SALT+SHADOW are clues a commercial word game would be pleased to ship. The method can clearly produce excellent clues; what it has not yet shown is that it can refuse to ship weak ones about itself.
